title: Remembering Stonewall
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the Stonewall Riots (Stonewall Uprising) of June 1969 at the Stonewall Inn in Greenwich Village, New York. They cover the repressive climate for gay and transgender people in the 1950s and 1960s (McCarthy-era persecution, anti-gay laws, the Lavender Scare, aversion therapy, the homophile movement and Mattachine Society), the Stonewall Inn's mafia ownership and police kickbacks from the Sixth Precinct, the June 28 1969 raid led by Deputy Inspector Seymour Pine, the crowd's resistance and the riot over the following days, and the aftermath including the first Pride march in 1970, the Compton's Cafeteria riot, and Stonewall's designation as a national monument. The episode opens with tour dates and closes with an iTunes review request.

segments.title: Tour dates and opening banter
segments.summary: The hosts read off their 2017 North American tour dates and benefit show, then introduce the episode on the Stonewall riots and mention the Stonewall Uprising documentary and a Grabster article.

segments.title: Stonewall's location and the hosts' experiences
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Stonewall Inn's location in the West Village of Greenwich Village and their own visits to the neighborhood, and Chuck describes visiting after the Pulse nightclub shooting, when the site became a gathering hub.

segments.title: Life for gay people in the 1950s and 1960s
segments.summary: The hosts describe the post-McCarthy low point for gay acceptance, anti-gay laws across states, gender-appropriate clothing laws used to arrest transgender people, police intimidation, violence, and the pressure to live closeted.

segments.title: Aversion therapy and the Lavender Scare
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the DSM classification of homosexuality as a mental illness, aversion therapy at Tascadero State Hospital including shock treatment and drugs, and the Lavender Scare under McCarthy.

segments.title: Homophile movement and the Mattachine Society
segments.summary: The hosts explain the quiet, respectable homophile movement that aimed to show gay people were normal, and the Mattachine Society, which founded newsletters and networks and held early public demonstrations in suits, though it was later criticized as too slow.

segments.title: Underground meeting places and the Stonewall Inn's history
segments.summary: The hosts explain that gay people lacked public meeting places and met in bathhouses, porn theaters, and meat trucks. They describe the Stonewall Inn's building history and its operation as a mafia-run gay bar with bad drinks and sanitation.

segments.title: Police kickbacks and the Sixth Precinct
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how the Sixth Precinct took bribes from the Stonewall owners, which allowed the bar to operate, and how periodic raids, ID checks on exit, and intimidation worked. They mention The Seven Five documentary.

segments.title: The June 1969 raid begins
segments.summary: The hosts describe the early morning raid led by Deputy Inspector Seymour Pine of the Division of Public Morals, the string of summer 1969 bar raids in Manhattan, and the reported influence of Judy Garland's death.

segments.title: The crowd resists and the riot begins
segments.summary: Patrons were checked on exit and a crowd gathered outside, including street kids and transgender people. Tensions rose and disputed accounts of who started the fighting were discussed, including Marcia Johnson and Jackie Hormona. Officers were stuck when backup did not arrive from the Sixth Precinct, and the crowd forced entry into the bar.

segments.title: Six days of rioting and the aftermath
segments.summary: The riot escalated with the Tactical Patrol Force called in and crowds of up to a thousand. Fighting continued for hours, and on later days the Black Panthers, hippies, and others joined. The Stonewall reopened, and protests calmed by the following Sunday. A commemorative march followed, and the first anniversary march became the first Pride parade.

segments.title: Legacy, Compton's Cafeteria, and national monument
segments.summary: The hosts discuss earlier uprisings such as Compton's Cafeteria in San Francisco, the Gay Liberation Front and Gay Liberation Front-era activism, the role of transgender people, criticism of the 2015 Stonewall film, and the Stonewall Inn's designation as a national monument.

segments.title: Sign-off and review request
segments.summary: The hosts ask listeners to leave iTunes reviews and share contact information and sign off.
